<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">costs and delays associated with developing software, documentation and training materials in multiple languages; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">political unrest, war or acts of terrorism occurring in the foreign countries in which we currently operate or intend to operate in the future.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We may not continue to succeed in developing and implementing policies and strategies that will be effective in each location where we currently do business or intend to do business in the future. Furthermore, the occurrence of any of the foregoing factors may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Insiders control a substantial amount of our outstanding stock, and this may delay or prevent a change of control of our company or adversely affect our stock price.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of February&nbsp;18, 2015, our executive officers, directors and affiliated entities together beneficially own approximately 36% of our common stock outstanding, including approximately 31% of our outstanding common stock held by our founder, Shawn McCreight, and his wife. As a result, these stockholders may have control over matters that require approval by our stockholders, including the election of directors and approval of significant corporate transactions. Corporate actions favored by these stockholders might be taken even if other stockholders oppose them. This concentration of ownership might also have the effect of delaying or preventing a change of control that other stockholders may view as beneficial.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our charter documents and Delaware law may deter potential acquirers of our business and may thus depress our stock price.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and our bylaws contain provisions that could delay or prevent a change of control of our company that our stockholders might consider favorable. In addition, we are governed by the provisions of Section&nbsp;203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, which may discourage, delay or prevent certain business combinations with stockholders owning 15% or more of our outstanding voting stock. These and other provisions in our charter documents may make it more difficult for stockholders or potential acquirers to initiate actions that are opposed by the then-current board of directors, including delaying or impeding a merger, tender offer, or proxy contest or other change of control transaction involving our company. Any delay or prevention of a change of control transaction could cause stockholders to lose a substantial premium over the then current market price of their shares.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">The trading price of our common stock is volatile.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The trading prices of the securities of technology companies have historically been highly volatile. Accordingly, the trading price of our common stock has been subject to wide fluctuations since our initial public offering in December&nbsp;2006. Factors that may affect the trading price of our common stock include:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">variations in our financial results;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.0pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">announcements of technological innovations, new solutions, pricing models, strategic alliances or significant agreements by us or by our competitors;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 49.0pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">recruitment or departure of key personnel;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">changes in the estimates of our financial results or changes in the recommendations of any securities analysts that elect to follow our common stock; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">market conditions in our industry, the industries of our customers and the economy as a whole.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, if the market for software or other technology stocks or the stock market in general experiences continued or greater loss of investor confidence, the trading price of our common stock could decline for reasons unrelated to our business or financial results. The trading price of our common stock might also decline in reaction to events that affect other companies in our industry even if these events do not directly affect us.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Future sales of shares by existing stockholders could cause our stock price to decline.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All of our outstanding shares are eligible for sale in the public market, subject in certain cases to volume limitations under Rule&nbsp;144 of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. Also, shares subject to outstanding options and rights under our Second Amended and Restated 2004 Equity Incentive Plan are eligible for sale in the public market to the extent permitted by the provisions of various vesting agreements and Rules&nbsp;144 and 701 under the Securities Act. If these shares are sold, or if it is perceived that they will be sold in the public market, the trading price of our common stock could decline.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, our founder, Shawn McCreight, and his wife, continue to hold a substantial number of shares of our common stock. Sales by Mr.&nbsp;McCreight or his wife of a substantial number of shares, or the expectation that such sales may occur, could significantly reduce the market price of our common stock.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Disruption in component supplies or a breakdown in the manufacturing supply chain could adversely impact hardware revenues.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tableau<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#153;</font>&#160; brand hardware products typically incorporate hundreds or more components from a wide range of manufacturing sources.&#160; In some cases these components are &#147;sole source&#148;, so it is possible for a disruption at a single supplier to constrain or entirely halt production of one of more Tableau brand products, perhaps for an extended period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, we use offshore contract manufacturing facilities for most of the assembly work related to Tableau brand hardware products.&#160; A breakdown in international transportation or political or economic upheaval could negatively impact our ability to manufacture or transport products leading to a loss of hardware product revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our balance sheet contained finite-lived intangible assets and goodwill totaling $22.4&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2014 that are subject to impairment review annually, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the value may not be recoverable, resulting in write-downs or write-offs. Such write-downs or write-offs could adversely impact our future earnings and stock price, our ability to obtain financing and our customer relationships.</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had $14.6&nbsp;million in indefinite-lived intangible assets and goodwill on our balance sheet. Accounting Standards Codification <i>Intangibles&nbsp;&#151; Goodwill and Other (ASC 350) </i>requires that goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets be tested for impairment annually, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the value may not be recoverable. Such testing could result in write-downs or write-offs to our goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets. Impairment is measured as the excess of the carrying value of the goodwill or intangible assets over the implied fair value of the underlying asset. Accordingly, we may, from time to time, incur impairment charges, which are recorded as operating expenses when they are incurred and would reduce our net income and adversely affect our operating results in the period in which they are incurred.&#160; One customer represents 47% of our subscription revenue for the year ended 2014.&#160; If we were to lose this specific customer, our subscription operations would be adversely affected, and this might result in an impairment of the goodwill and intangible assets in this reporting unit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had $7.8&nbsp;million of other net intangible assets, consisting of core technology, existing and developed technology, customer relationships and tradenames that we amortize over time. Any material impairment to any of these items could adversely affect our results of operations and could affect the trading price of our common stock in the period in which they are incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.45pt;text-indent:-55.45pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;1B.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Unresolved Staff Comments</font></b><a name="Item1b_UnresolvedStaffComments_132945"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.45pt;text-indent:-55.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-55.1pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;2.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Properties</font></b><a name="Ties_132948"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-55.1pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our corporate headquarters is located in Pasadena, California.&#160; From January&nbsp;to July&nbsp;of 2013, we leased approximately 70,000 square feet in two locations.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In July&nbsp;2012, we entered into an Office Lease Agreement (the &#147;Lease&#148;) to lease approximately 90,000 rentable square feet of an office building, also located in Pasadena, California.&#160; The Lease began on August&nbsp;1, 2013 and has an initial term of ten years and ten months.&#160; The Lease allowed the Company to consolidate its Pasadena operations into a single location.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also lease approximately 62,000 square feet at facilities in: Houston, Texas; New York City, New York; Waukesha, Wisconsin; San Francisco, California; Dulles, Virginia; Chicago,&nbsp;Illinois; Orlando, Florida, Chandler, Arizona and near London, England.&#160; We also maintain regional facilities in Singapore and Brazil.&#160; These leases expire at various points through 2019.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-55.1pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;3.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Legal Proceedings</font></b><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_132957"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-55.1pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;20, 2011, MyKey Technology Inc. (&#147;MyKey&#148;) filed a complaint against us and certain other parties for patent infringement in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware.&#160; With respect to the Company, the complaint alleged that certain of our data acquisition forensic hardware products that we acquired as a result of our acquisition of certain assets of Tableau, LLC (&#147;Tableau&#148;) infringe three of MyKey&#146;s patents relating to write blocking, duplication and data removal technologies, respectively.&#160; The complaint sought a declaration of infringement, a finding of willful infringement, compensatory damages, treble damages, injunctive relief, interest, expenses, costs and attorneys&#146; fees.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;22, 2011, MyKey also filed a complaint with the United States International Trade Commission (the &#147;ITC&#148;), alleging infringement by the Company and certain other parties of the three patents discussed in the preceding paragraph and requesting that the ITC commence an investigation pursuant to Section&nbsp;337 of the Tariff Act of 1930.&#160; The complaint sought injunctive relief barring the Company from the importation of products that allegedly infringed the three patents of MyKey.&#160; On August&nbsp;24, 2011, the ITC commenced an investigation of the Company and certain other parties related to the complaint by MyKey.&#160; On August&nbsp;31, 2011 the proceeding in the District Court was stayed pending the resolution of the ITC matter.&#160; On August&nbsp;1, 2012, MyKey amended its ITC complaint to remove allegations that its duplication patent had been infringed by the Company and to reduce the number of claims it alleges the Company has infringed related to MyKey&#146;s data removal patent.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2012, the parties completed a trial on the remaining patent claims at issue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;28, 2012, the ITC released a final determination and Order holding that no violation of Section&nbsp;337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 occurred as a result of the Company&#146;s importation into the United States and sale of the products at issue.&#160; This Order effectively ended the ITC proceeding in the Company&#146;s favor.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;20, 2013, the U.S. District Court of Delaware lifted the stay of the proceedings in the MyKey matter.&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective April&nbsp;8, 2013, the parties stipulated to a transfer of the matter to the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.&#160; On April&nbsp;16, 2013, the Company filed its Answer and Counterclaim.&#160; MyKey filed a petition to consolidate a number of related cases, including the case against the Company in the Central District of California, into a Multi-District Litigation (&#147;MDL&#148;) proceeding.&#160; On August&nbsp;16, 2013, the MDL panel approved the petition and assigned the MDL consolidated cases to the judge who is also presiding over the individual case against the Company.&#160; The MDL case will dispose of certain issues common to the consolidated cases, such as the validity of patents being asserted against the joint defendants.&#160; On May&nbsp;23, 2014, the parties completed a Markman hearing related to claim construction of the patents at issue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;26, 2014, MyKey also filed a complaint against the United States of America alleging that the United States has infringed U.S. Patents No.&nbsp;6,813,682, 7,159,086 and 7,228,379 by or through its acceptance, receipt and/or use of write blocker products, data duplication products and data removal products.&#160; The complaint alleges that such products were supplied to the government by the Company and certain of its co-defendants in the MDL proceeding.&#160; No damages amount is stated in the complaint.&#160; The government could assert a claim for indemnification against the Company but has not done so yet.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;16, 2014, MyKey filed a Notice of Status on Claim Construction Issues in which it acknowledged that MyKey will not be able to prove that the Company&#146;s data duplication products infringed U.S. Patent 7,159,086.&#160; In the same filing, MyKey acknowledged that certain claims of United States Patent 6,813,682 are invalid and therefore cannot be infringed by any product.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We intend to defend the remaining MyKey matters vigorously and, at this time, are unable to estimate what, if any, liability we may have in connection with these matters.&#160; Although a financial loss is reasonably possible from currently pending MyKey cases, the Company is unable to estimate a range of reasonably possible financial losses due to various reasons, including, among others, that (1)&nbsp;certain of the proceedings are still at an early stage, (2)&nbsp;there is uncertainty as to the outcome of pending appeals, motions, or settlements, (3)&nbsp;there are significant factual issues to be resolved, (4)&nbsp;there are unresolved negotiations with certain indemnitors or indemnitees of the Company, related to the actions, and (5)&nbsp;we have meritorious defenses that we intend to assert.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, we may become involved in various other lawsuits and legal proceedings that arise in the ordinary course</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> of business.&#160; Litigation is subject to inherent uncertainties, and an adverse result in these or other matters may arise from time to time that may harm our business.&#160; We are not currently aware of any such other legal proceedings or claims that are likely to have a material impact on our business.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of January&nbsp;31, 2015, there were 19 holders of record of our common stock.&#160; On February&nbsp;18, 2015, the last sale price reported on the NASDAQ Global Market for our common stock was $6.16 per share.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We anticipate that any future earnings will be retained to finance continuing development of our business. Accordingly, we do not anticipate paying dividends on our common stock in the foreseeable future. Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon our results of operation, financial condition and other factors as the Board of Directors, in its discretion, deems relevant.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Purchases of Equity Securities by the Issuer</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2008, our Board of Directors authorized a program to repurchase shares of our common stock having an aggregate value of up to $8.0 million. As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had approximately $3.6 million remaining under this authorization. The authorization allows us to repurchase our common stock from time to time through open market purchases and negotiated transactions, or otherwise. There were no open market purchases during 2014, 2013, or 2012. The timing, nature and amount of such transactions will depend on a variety of factors, including market conditions, and the program may be suspended, discontinued or accelerated at any time. The sources of funds for the purchases under the remaining authorization are our existing cash on hand and cash from operations. Purchases are made in the open market, through block trades and other negotiated transactions. Repurchased shares are held in Treasury Stock and have not been retired.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee transactions listed in the table below consist of shares withheld by the Company to satisfy employee personal income tax withholding requirements upon the vesting of share awards issued under our equity compensation plans.&#160; Withholdings are limited to minimum statutory requirements.&#160; As of January&nbsp;2014, the Company no longer withholds shares to satisfy employee personal income tax withholding requirements upon vesting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following graph illustrates a comparison of the total cumulative stockholder return on our common stock for each of the last five fiscal years with two indices: (i)&nbsp;the NASDAQ Composite Index (symbol: ^IXIC) and (ii)&nbsp;the NASDAQ Computer Index (symbol: ^IXCO). The graph assumes an initial investment of $100 at the beginning of the five year period and that all dividends have been reinvested.&#160; No cash dividends have been declared on our common stock.&#160; The quotes were obtained from http://finance.yahoo.com. The comparisons in the graph are required by the SEC and are not intended to forecast or be indicative of the possible future performance of our common stock.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.5pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Non-cash compensation recorded for each of the last five years five years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 relates to stock options and restricted stock granted to employees measured under the fair value method and includes costs related to nonvested share grants.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.5pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-54.1pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;7.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</font></b><a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_133113"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 55.1pt;text-indent:-55.1pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations should be read together with the financial statements and related notes that are included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K. This discussion may contain forward-looking statements based upon current expectations that involve risks and uncertainties.&#160; Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including those set forth under &#147;Risk Factors&#148; or in other parts of this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We develop and provide the leading software and hardware solutions for digital investigations, including EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise, a network-enabled product primarily for corporations and government agencies, and EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic, a desktop-based product primarily for law enforcement agencies and digital investigators.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We were incorporated and commenced operations in 1997.&#160; From 1997 through 2002, we generated a substantial portion of our revenues from the sale of our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic products and related services.&#160; We have experienced increases in our revenue as a result of the release of our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise product in late 2002, which expanded our customer base into corporate enterprises and federal government agencies.&#160; In addition, the releases of our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;eDiscovery solution in late 2005 and EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Information Assurance solution in late 2006 (which was replaced by our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Cybersecurity solution in 2009) have increased our revenues.&#160; In May&nbsp;2010, we added a family of data acquisition forensic hardware products including forensic duplicators, multiple write blockers and other hardware through our acquisition of Tableau, LLC (&#147;Tableau&#148;).&#160; In February&nbsp;2012, we added cloud-based document review and production software-as-a-service for corporations and law firms through our acquisition of CaseCentral,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; In September&nbsp;2013, we introduced EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>Analytics, a security intelligence solution that exposes threats that evade detection using insights from endpoint data.&#160; We anticipate that sales of our EnCase Enterprise products and related services, in particular our EnCase Cybersecurity and EnCase eDiscovery solutions, sales of our forensic hardware products and sales of subscriptions for cloud-based document review and production SaaS will comprise a substantial portion of our future revenues.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Important Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are a number of trends that may affect our business and our industry.&#160; We have identified factors that we expect to play an important role in our future growth and profitability.&#160; Some of these trends or other factors include:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Legislative and regulatory developments. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our digital investigation solutions allow law enforcement agencies, government organizations and corporations to conduct investigations within the legal and regulatory framework.&#160; Historically, the implementation of new laws and regulations surrounding digital investigations has helped create demand for our products. Future changes in applicable laws or regulations could enhance or detract from the desirability of our products.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Information technology budgets. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deployment of our solutions may require a substantial capital expenditure by our customers.&#160; Budgets for information technology-related capital expenditures at corporations and all levels of government organizations are typically cyclical in nature, with generally higher budgets in times of improving economic conditions and lower budgets in times of economic slowdowns.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Law enforcement agency budgets.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> We sell our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic products and training services primarily to law enforcement agencies.&#160; Because of the limited nature of law enforcement budgets, funds are typically initially allocated toward solving issues perceived to be the most pressing.&#160; Sales of our products could be impacted by changes in the budgets of law enforcement agencies or in the relative priority assigned to digital law enforcement investigations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Prevalence and impact of security breaches, hacking incidents and spread of malicious software.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> The increasing sophistication of security breaches and hacking attacks on government and private networks and the global spread of malicious software, such as viruses, worms and rootkits, have increased the focus of corporations and large government organizations on digital investigations and other aspects of network security, which has, in turn, increased demand for our products.&#160; Future changes in the number and severity of such breaches, attacks or the spread of malicious software could have an effect on the demand for our products.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">28<a name="PB_28_124206_141"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Seasonality in revenues.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> We experience seasonality in our revenues, with the third and fourth quarters typically having the highest revenues for the year.&#160; We believe that this seasonality results primarily from our customers&#146; budgeting cycles.&#160; The federal government budget year ends in the third calendar quarter of the year and a majority of corporate budget years end in the fourth calendar quarter of the year.&#160; In addition, our customers also tend to make software purchases near the end of a particular quarter, which tends to make our revenues for a particular period unpredictable for a significant portion of that period.&#160; We expect that this seasonality within particular years and unpredictability within particular quarterly periods will continue for the foreseeable future.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Amount of commercial litigation.</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Because commercial litigation often involves e-discovery, an increase in commercial litigation could increase demand for our products and services, while a decrease in commercial litigation could decrease demand.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Summary of Results of Operations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our total revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 was $108.7 million, a decrease of $1.9 million, or 2%, from 2013.&#160; Product revenue was $34.4 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, an increase&#160; of $0.2 million, or 1%, from 2013.&#160; Subscription revenue was $7.4 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, a decrease of $2.9 million, or 28%, from 2013.&#160; Services and maintenance revenues was $66.8 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, an increase of $0.9 million, or 1%, from 2013.&#160; The decrease in our total revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, compared to 2013 was primarily due to a decrease in subscription revenue, partially offset by small increases in product and services and maintenance revenues.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our net loss for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 was $14.7 million, or $0.55 per share, compared to a net loss of $21.5 million, or $0.83 per share, for 2013.&#160; Our future profitability is primarily dependent upon revenue from the sale of our products.&#160; The primary contributors to the decrease in our net loss for 2014 were a decrease in cost of revenues and operating expenses compared with 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Sources of Revenue</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our software product sales</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> transactions typically include the following elements: (i)&nbsp;a software license fee paid for the use of our products under a perpetual license term, or for a specific term; (ii)&nbsp;an arrangement for first-year support and maintenance, which includes unspecified software updates, upgrades and post-contract support; (iii)&nbsp;and professional services for installation, implementation, consulting and training. With our acquisition of CaseCentral in February&nbsp;2012, we began to generate revenue from cloud-based document review and production software sold as subscription services. We sell our software products and services through our direct sales force, our inside sales force and in some cases we utilize resellers. We sell our hardware products primarily through resellers.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Product Revenue</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We generate product revenue principally from two product categories: Enterprise products and Forensic products.&#160; Our Enterprise products include revenue related to licenses of our EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Cybersecurity, and EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174; </font>eDiscovery sales.&#160; Our Forensic products include revenue related to EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174; </font>Portable, and forensic hardware sales.&#160; During the first two quarters of each fiscal year, we typically experience our lowest levels of product sales due to the seasonal budgetary cycles of our customers.&#160; The third quarter is typically the strongest quarter for sales to our federal government customers. Typically, sales to our corporate customers are highest in the fourth quarter.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">29<a name="PB_29_125046_7608"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Product revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 increased $0.2 million, or 1%, to $34.4 million from $34.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase was due to a $1.1 million increase, or 11%, to $10.7 million from $9.6 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013,&#160; in hardware revenues due to new versions of our hardware products being released, partially offset by a $0.9 million decrease, or 8%, to $9.9 million from $10.8 million, in forensic products revenues resulting from continued weakness in spending by our government customers.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 we added 568 new EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise customers, as compared to 278 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Product revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 decreased $21.9 million, or 39%, to $34.2 million from $56.1 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The decrease was due to a decrease in both Enterprise and Forensic revenues.&nbsp; Enterprise product revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 decreased by $16.1 million, or 54%, to $13.8 million from $29.9 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 primarily due to significantly reduced spending by government customers as a result of the federal budget sequestration.&#160; During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 we added 278 new EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise customers, as compared to 358 for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; During 2013, 66% of Enterprise product revenue was the result of sales to existing customers, compared to 74% in 2012.&#160; Forensic revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 decreased by $5.8 million, or 22%, to $20.4 million from $26.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, primarily due to significantly reduced spending by our government customers impacted by the federal budget sequestration.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Subscription Revenue</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subscription service customers have the right to access our cloud-based document review and production software; however, they may not take possession of the software at any time during the term of their agreement.&#160; We generate subscription revenue principally from two types of customers: corporate or large enterprise customers who typically use our cloud-based software to host multiple legal cases on an ongoing basis, and law firm customers, who typically use our cloud-based software to host single cases.&#160; In general, we recognize revenues for subscriptions on a straight-line basis over the contract period commencing on the date the subscription is made available to the customer.&#160; Usage-based fees, which are determined monthly, are recognized when incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subscription revenue from our cloud-based document review and production software for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 decreased $2.9 million, or 28%, to $7.4 million from $10.3 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily due to downward pricing pressure in the eDiscovery sector and reduced revenue as a result of single-use law firm customers transitioning their cases from production to archive status. Our business model focuses on corporate or enterprise customers who typically use our product for multiple legal cases on an ongoing basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subscription revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $1.1 million, or 12%, to $10.3 million from $9.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The increase is primarily due to our CaseCentral acquisition in February&nbsp;2012, when we began to generate revenues from software sold as subscription services.&#160; Subscription revenue for 2013 includes a full year of subscription revenue as compared to a partial year of subscription revenue for 2012, since we started generating subscription revenue in February&nbsp;2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Services and Maintenance Revenues</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 increased $0.8 million, or 1%, to $66.8 million from $66.0 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily due to a $2.1 million increase in maintenance revenues as a result of sustained increases in our installed product base and customers desiring to continue maintenance support on our products, partially offset by a $1.3 million decrease in professional services due to a decrease in case work and incident response work for our cloud-based subscriptions due to lower demand for our services from hosting customers. In 2014, our installed product base increased primarily through the addition of 568 new EnCase Enterprise customers, and sales of 137 new EnCase eDiscovery, 157 new EnCase Cybersecurity, and 99 new EnCase Analytics modules to existing EnCase Enterprise customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $1.8 million, or 3%, to $66.0 million from $64.2 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; Service revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $0.3 million, or 1%, to $28.2 million from $27.9 million, for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, primarily due to an increase of $1.3 million in case work, incident response work and implementation work for customers of our EnCase Enterprise products, as well as an increase of approximately $0.8 million in professional services related to the timing of our acquisition of CaseCentral in February&nbsp;2012, partially offset by a decrease of $1.0 million in training revenue due to reduced</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">30<a name="PB_30_125156_8146"></a></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">spending by our government customers impacted by the federal budget sequestration.&#160; Maintenance revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $1.5 million, or 4%, to $37.8 million from $36.3 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 primarily due to sustained increases in our product base and high annual renewal rates by customers desiring maintenance support on our products.&#160; In 2013 our installed product base increased primarily through the addition of 278 new EnCase Enterprise customers, and sales of 35 new EnCase Cybersecurity, 38 new EnCase e-Discovery, and 5 EnCase Analytics modules to existing EnCase Enterprise customers.</font></p>

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">66.1</font></p>    </td>
<td width="2%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 2.25pt 0in;width:2.5%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">%</font></p>    </td>
<td width="10%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:10.0%;">

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">71.9</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 2.25pt 0in;width:1.0%;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cost of Product Revenue</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost of product revenue consists principally of the cost of producing our software products, the cost of manufacturing our hardware products and product distribution costs, including the cost of packaging, shipping, customs duties, and compensation and related overhead expenses.&#160; While these costs are primarily variable with respect to sales volumes, they remain low in relation to the revenue generated and result in higher gross margins than our subscription and services and maintenance businesses.&#160; Our gross margins can be affected by product mix, as our enterprise products are generally higher margin products than our forensic products, which include software and hardware.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Costs of product revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 increased $1.0 million, or 13%, to $8.4 million from $7.5 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily due to a $0.8 million increase in hardware costs and a $0.3 million increase in Original Equipment Manufacturer (&#147;OEM&#148;) royalty expense associated with higher sales of hardware.&#160; Product gross margin decreased to 75.5% in 2014 from 78.2% in 2013 primarily due to the increase in hardware sales which have a lower gross margin than our enterprise and forensic software sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Cost of product revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 decreased $0.5 million, or 6%, to $7.5 million from $8.0 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The decrease was primarily a result of a decrease in the cost of forensic hardware of approximately $0.9 million, offset by approximately $0.2 million increase in custom duty expense due to increased international sales and a $0.2 million increase in OEM royalty expense.&#160; Product gross margin decreased to 78.2% in 2013 from 85.8% in 2012 primarily due to the decrease in enterprise and forensic software revenues, which have higher gross margins than forensic hardware sales.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">31<a name="PB_31_125627_7091"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cost of Subscription Revenue</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of subscription revenue consists principally of employee compensation costs, including share-based compensation and related overhead, software maintenance paid to third party vendors, and SaaS hosting infrastructure costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of subscription revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 increased $0.3 million, or 6%, to $4.6 million from $4.3 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The increase was primarily due to rent expense related to our data center which increased $0.7 million, partially offset by a $0.4 million reduction in employee-related costs due to the reduction in headcount. Subscription gross margin decreased to 38.2% in 2014 from 58.3% in 2013 primarily due to subscription revenues decreasing by 28%, while the cost of subscription revenue increased by 6%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of subscription revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $0.6 million, or 16%, to $4.3 million from $3.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The increase for the year was primarily due to the cloud-based document and production software products not becoming a part of our product mix until the completion of our acquisition of CaseCentral in February&nbsp;2012.&#160; The year end results for 2013 include a full year of costs of subscription revenue as compared to a partial year of costs of subscription revenue for 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cost of Services and Maintenance Revenues</font></i></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of services and maintenance revenues are largely comprised of employee compensation costs, including share-based compensation, and related overhead, travel and facilities costs.&#160; The cost of maintenance revenue is primarily outsourced, but also includes employee compensation costs for customer technical support and related overhead costs.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 decreased $2.8 million, or 11%, to $23.0 million from $25.8 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; The decrease was primarily due to a $2.6 million decrease in cost of professional services due to a decrease in compensation and related expenses associated with a reduction in headcount.&#160; Services and maintenance gross margin was 65.6% in 2014, compared to 61.0% in 2013.&#160; The higher gross margin was primarily a result of services revenues decreasing by only 4%, while the cost of services decreased by 12%.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 increased $1.1 million, or 4%, to $25.8 million from $24.7 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.&#160; The increase in the cost of services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, from 2012 was primarily due to an increase in costs of professional services.&#160; The increased costs included compensation and related expenses associated with higher revenues and related travel.&#160; Additionally, approximately $0.6 million of the increase in cost of services and maintenance revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013 was due to a full year of costs related to the acquisition of CaseCentral, whereas only a partial year of costs were captured in 2012.&#160; Services and maintenance gross margin was 61.0% in 2013, compared to 61.4% in 2012.&#160; The lower services and maintenance gross margin for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013, from 2012, was primarily a result of training revenue decreasing by 10%, while the cost of training increased slightly.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Operating Expenses</font></i></b></p>
