<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2014, the FASB and IASB jointly issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09, <i>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</i>, which supercedes the revenue recognition requirements in ASC 605 Revenue Recognition.&#160; ASU 2014-09 is a comprehensive new revenue recognition standard that will supercede nearly all existing revenue recognition guidance under US GAAP.&#160; The standard&#146;s core principle is that a company will recognize revenue when it transfers promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&#160; In doing so, companies will need to use more judgment and make more estimates than under current authoritative guidance.&#160; These may include identifying performance obligations in the contract, estimating the amount of variable consideration to include in the transaction price and allocating the transaction price to each separate performance obligation.&#160; The standard is effective beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016, and early adoption is not permitted under US GAAP.&#160; We are currently evaluating the financial statement impact of the new revenue recognition standard.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15,&nbsp;<i>Presentation of Financial Statements-Going Concern&nbsp;(Subtopic 205-40),&nbsp;Disclosure of Uncertainties about an Entity&#146;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern.</i>&nbsp;This standard sets forth management&#146;s responsibility to evaluate, each reporting period, whether there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern, and if so, to provide related footnote disclosures. The standard is effective for annual and interim reporting periods ending after December&nbsp;15, 2016. &nbsp;We are currently evaluating this new standard and expect it to have no impact on our financial position and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Non-Audit Services of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Audit Committee of the Board of Directors has pre-approved all non-audit services including tax compliance services.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp;7A.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures about Market Risk</font></b><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_125827"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Market Risk. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Market risk represents the risk of loss that may impact our financial position due to adverse changes in the financial market prices and rates.&#160; Our market risk exposure is primarily a result of fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, interest rates and credit risk. We do not hold or issue financial instruments for trading purposes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Foreign Currency Risk. </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To date, substantially all of our international sales have been denominated in US dollars, and therefore, the majority of our revenues are not subject to foreign currency risk.&#160; Our operating expenses and cash flows are subject to fluctuations due to changes in foreign currency exchange rates, but historically have had relatively little impact on our operating results and cash flows.&#160; A strengthening of the dollar could make our products and services less competitive in foreign markets and therefore could reduce our revenues.&#160; In the future, an increased portion of our revenues and costs may be denominated in foreign currencies.&#160; We do not enter into derivative instrument transactions for trading or speculative purposes.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Interest Rate Risk.&#160; </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our investment portfolio, consisting of highly liquid debt instruments of the US government at December&nbsp;31, 2014, is subject to interest rate risk.&#160; The fair value of our investment portfolio would not be significantly impacted by either a 100 basis point increase or decrease in interest rates due mainly to the short-term nature of the major portion of our investment portfolio.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 8.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font></b><a name="Item8_FinancialStatementsAndSuppl_125830"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our financial statements and supplementary data are included at the end of this report, beginning on page&nbsp;F-1.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp; 9A.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Controls and Procedures</font></b><a name="Item9a_ControlsAndProcedures_125008"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management, with the participation of the interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, has performed an evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934).&#160; This evaluation includes consideration of the controls, processes and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports we file under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s rules&nbsp;and forms and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.&#160; Based on such evaluation, our interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Management Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)&nbsp;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.&#160; Our internal control over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160; Our internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(i)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of our assets;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(ii)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that our receipts and expenditures are being made only in accordance with authorizations of our management and directors; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(iii)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of our assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any system of internal control, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention or overriding of controls.&#160; Accordingly, even an effective internal control system may not prevent or detect misstatements and can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation.&#160; Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, utilizing the criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (COSO) in <i>Internal Controls&#151;Integrated Framework</i><i>.</i>&#160; Based on the results of this assessment, management (including our interim Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer) has concluded that, as of that date, our internal control over financial reporting was effective.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The attestation report concerning the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, issued by our independent registered public accounting firm, Ernst and Young,&nbsp;LLP, is included under Item 9B.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There have been no changes in our internal control over financial reporting during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2014 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal controls over financial reporting.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .75in;text-indent:-.75in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item&nbsp; 9B.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Other Information</font></b><a name="Item9b_OtherInformation_125010"></a></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.&#146;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on criteria established in Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.&#146;s management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying Management Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appearing under Item&nbsp;9A. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1)&nbsp;pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3)&nbsp;provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the company&#146;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on the COSO criteria<b>.</b></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheet of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity and cash flows for each of the two years in the ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. and our report dated February&nbsp;24, 2015 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">/s/ Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font></b><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_161639"></a></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheet of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, and the related consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity and cash flows for each of the two years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014. Our audit also included the financial statements schedule listed in the Index at Item 15(a)(2).&#160; These financial statements and schedule are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements and schedule based on our audits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. at December&nbsp;31, 2014, and the consolidated results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the two years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.&#160; Also, in our opinion, the related financial statements schedule, when considered in relation to the basic financial statements taken as a whole, presents fairly in all material respects the information set forth therein.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.&#146;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2014, based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) and our report dated February&nbsp;24, 2015 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To the Board of Directors and Stockholders of</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pasadena, California</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated statements of operations, stockholders&#146; equity, and cash flows of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;) for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. Our audit also included the financial statement schedule for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 listed in the Index at Item 15. These financial statements and financial statement schedule are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the financial statements and financial statement schedule based on our audit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, such consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the results of Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. and subsidiaries&#146; operations and their cash flows for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also, in our opinion, such financial statement schedule, when considered in relation to the basic consolidated financial statements taken as a whole, present fairly, in all material respects, the information set forth therein.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">GUIDANCE SOFTWARE,&nbsp;INC.</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b><a name="NotesToConsolidatedFinancialState_161852"></a></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Description of the Business</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. was incorporated in the state of California in 1997 and reincorporated in Delaware on December&nbsp;11, 2006.&#160; Guidance and its subsidiaries are collectively referred to herein as &#147;Guidance,&#148; &#147;we,&#148; &#147;our,&#148; or the &#147;Company.&#148; Headquartered in Pasadena, California, Guidance is a global provider of software and hardware solutions to conduct digital investigations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our main products are: <i>EnCase</i><font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><i>&#160;Enterprise</i>, a comprehensive, network-enabled digital investigative solution that enables corporations and government agencies to search, collect, preserve and analyze data across all of the servers, desktops and laptops that comprise their entire network from a single location;&#160; <i>EnCase</i><font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><i>&#160;eDiscovery</i>, which automates the search, collection, preservation and processing of electronically stored information for litigation and compliance purposes; <i>EnCase</i><font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><i>&#160;Cybersecurity</i>, which provides the ability to identify potential threats and analyze them, identify other advanced hacking techniques that evade traditional network or host-based defenses, provides investigative capabilities that target confidential or sensitive data, and mitigates risk by removing sensitive data from unauthorized locations;&#160; <i>EnCase</i><font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><i>&#160;Forensic</i>, a desktop-based product primarily used by law enforcement and government agencies for collecting, preserving, analyzing and authenticating electronic computer forensic data for use in criminal and civil court proceedings.&#160; In 2009, we launched <i>EnCase</i><font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font><i>&#160;Portable</i>, a data acquisition solution that enables customers to leverage the search and acquisition capabilities of EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;software in a wide range of field applications through the use of a portable device and in May&nbsp;2010, we added a family of data acquisition forensic hardware products including forensic duplicators, multiple write blockers and other hardware through our acquisition of Tableau, LLC (&#147;Tableau&#148;).&#160; In February&nbsp;2012, we added cloud-based document review and production software-as-a-service for corporations and law firms through our acquisition of CaseCentral,&nbsp;Inc.&#160; In September&nbsp;2013, we added <i>EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Analytics</i>, a security intelligence product designed to derive insights from the data generated by endpoint activity.&#160; In addition, we complement our offerings with a comprehensive array of professional and training services including technical support and maintenance services to help our customers implement our solutions, conduct investigations and train their IT and legal professionals to effectively and efficiently use our products.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Basis of Presentation</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (&#147;GAAP&#148;), and include the accounts of Guidance and its wholly owned subsidiaries.&#160; All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Prior Period Correction</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the Company&#146;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for 2013 the Company disclosed that subsequent to the issuance of the 2012 consolidated financial statements, management concluded that certain share data had been incorrectly reported.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s restricted stock award agreements provide that holders of the restricted stock awards shall have all the rights of a stockholder upon the grant date, including the right to vote as a stockholder.&nbsp; As such, these shares are considered issued and outstanding on the date of grant.&nbsp; Historically, the Company excluded unvested restricted stock awards from the presented quantity of common shares issued and outstanding.&nbsp; The table below highlights the previously reported common stock balances and corrections necessary to reflect the restricted stock awards as issued and outstanding upon the grant date (in thousands).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Use of Estimates and Assumptions</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities.&#160; On an ongoing basis, we evaluate these estimates, including those related to revenue recognition, share-based compensation, bad debts, income taxes, contingent consideration, goodwill and long-lived asset impairment, non-monetary transactions, commitments, contingencies and litigation.&#160; We base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances.&#160; Actual results may differ from these estimates.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We invest excess cash in money market funds and highly liquid debt instruments of the US government and its agencies.&#160; Highly liquid investments with stated maturities of three months or less from the date of purchase are classified as cash and cash equivalents.</font></p>

<div>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Restricted Cash</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had $0.2 million of restricted cash held as collateral on outstanding letters of credit, related to our San Francisco office lease.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value of Financial Instruments</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying amounts of cash equivalents, accounts receivable, and accounts payable approximate fair value because of the short-term maturities of these instruments.&#160; Based on borrowing rates currently available to us for borrowings with similar terms, the carrying values of our capital lease obligations also approximate fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Trade Receivables</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Trade receivables are carried at original invoice amount less an allowance for doubtful accounts.&#160; The allowance is established through a provision for bad debt expense.&#160; We determine the adequacy of this allowance by evaluating individual customer accounts receivable, through consideration of the customer&#146;s financial condition, credit history and current economic conditions.&#160; In addition, we analyze our historical credit loss history and apply these loss rates to our current accounts receivable balances to verify the reasonableness of our allowance.&#160; Trade receivables are written off when deemed uncollectible.&#160; A trade receivable is generally considered past due if any portion of the receivable balance is outstanding for more than 30 days unless alternate terms are provided.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Inventory</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inventory is comprised of hardware components, packaged software components and finished goods and is valued at the lower of cost or market, using the weighted average cost method.&#160; We conduct quarterly inventory reviews for obsolescence, and inventory considered unlikely to be sold is adjusted to net realizable value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Business Combinations</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The purchase price of an acquisition is allocated to the underlying assets acquired and liabilities assumed based upon their estimated fair values at the date of acquisition.&#160; To the extent the purchase price exceeds the fair value of the net identifiable tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed, such excess is allocated to goodwill.&#160; We determine the estimated fair values after review and consideration of relevant information including discounted cash flows, quoted market prices and estimates made by management.&#160; Accordingly, these can be affected by certain performance measurements and other factors over time, which may cause final amounts to differ materially from original estimates.&#160; We adjust the preliminary purchase price allocation, as necessary, up to periods of one year after the acquisition closing date as we obtain more information regarding asset valuations and liabilities assumed.&#160; We refer to this preliminary purchase price allocation period as the measurement period.&#160; Goodwill acquired in business combinations is assigned to the reporting unit(s)&nbsp;expected to benefit from the combination as of the acquisition date.&#160; Acquisition related costs are recognized separately from the acquisition and are expensed as incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Property and Equipment</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The cost of property and equipment, less applicable estimated residual values, is depreciated over the shorter of their estimated useful lives or the life of the lease (if applicable), on the straight-line method, from the date the specific asset is completed, installed, and ready for use, as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We review our long-lived assets for impairment in accordance with <i>Property, Plant and Equipment (ASC 360)</i>.&#160; Long-lived assets are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable.&#160; Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of the assets to future net cash flows (undiscounted and without interest) expected to be generated by the asset.&#160; If such assets are considered to be impaired, the impairment to be recognized is measured by the amount by which the carrying amount of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets.&#160; Assets to be disposed of are reported at the lower of the carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell.&#160; To date, we have not determined that any of our long-lived assets have been impaired.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Amortization of Intangible Assets with Finite Lives</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Intangible assets with finite lives are recorded at the fair value of such assets at the time of acquisition.&#160; With the exception of our customer relationships intangible assets, which are amortized on a double-declining basis, the acquisition date fair value of such assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Goodwill and Indefinite-Lived Intangibles</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Goodwill represents the excess of purchase price over fair value of net assets acquired and is assigned to a reporting unit at the date the goodwill is initially recorded.&#160; Goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets are not amortized but evaluated for impairment annually, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the value may not be recoverable.&#160; Commencing on January&nbsp;1, 2013, the Company adopted the ASU 2011-08 issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) for the revised guidance on &#147;Testing of Goodwill for Impairment.&#148;&#160; Under this guidance, the Company has the option to choose whether it will apply the qualitative assessment first before the quantitative assessment.&#160; If a quantitative assessment is necessary a two-step test is performed at the reporting unit level to assess goodwill for impairment.&#160;&#160;&#160; First, the fair value of the reporting unit is compared to its carrying value.&#160; If the fair value exceeds the carrying value, the reporting unit is not impaired and no further testing is performed.&#160; The second step is performed if the carrying value exceeds the fair value.&#160; If the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeds its implied fair value, an impairment loss equal to the difference will be recorded.&#160; Indefinite-lived intangible assets are assessed for impairment by comparing the carrying value of the assets with their fair values.&#160; If the carrying value of an indefinite-lived intangible asset exceeds its implied fair value, an impairment loss equal to the difference will be recorded.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Application of the impairment test requires significant judgment to estimate the fair value.&#160; Changes in estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and/or impairment.&#160; See Note 7 &#151; Goodwill and Other Intangibles.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.35in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial instruments that potentially subject us to significant concentrations of credit risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents and accounts receivable.&#160; We restrict our investments in cash and cash equivalents to financial institutions, US government or federal agency instruments and obligations of corporations with high credit standing.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, the majority of our cash balances were held at financial institutions located in California, in accounts that are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation up to $250,000.&#160; Uninsured balances aggregate approximately $18.0 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, all of our cash equivalents consisted of financial institution obligations.&#160; We periodically perform credit evaluations of our customers and maintain reserves for potential losses on our accounts receivable.&#160; We do not believe we are subject to concentrations of credit risk with respect to such receivables.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.35in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We generate revenues principally from the sale of our EnCase&#174; Enterprise and EnCase&#174; Forensic software products.&#160; Our Enterprise products include perpetual licenses and are related to our EnCase&#174; Enterprise, EnCase&#174; Cybersecurity, and eDiscovery products.&#160; Our Forensic products include revenues related to EnCase&#174; Forensic, EnCase&#174; Portable, and forensic hardware sales.&#160; Revenue associated with the sale of software licenses and revenue associated with forensic hardware sales are referred to as product revenue.&#160; Revenue associated with cloud-based document review and production software-as-a-service which is referred to as subscription revenue.&#160; Revenues are also generated from training courses, implementation services and consulting services in which we assist customers with the performance of digital investigations and train their IT and legal professionals in the use of our software products, which we collectively refer to as services revenues.&#160; Our proprietary products are generally sold with one to three years of maintenance, which can be renewed at a stated renewal rate and is referred to as maintenance revenues.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-10<a name="PB_10_125419_5796"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We recognize revenue in accordance with Accounting Standards Update (&#147;ASU&#148;) 2009-13, <i>Multiple-Deliverable Revenue Arrangement</i>s, (amendment to Accounting Standards Codification (&#147;ASC&#148;) Topic 605, <i>Revenue Recognition</i>), <i>Revenue Recognition - Software</i> topic (ASC 985-605) and <i>Revenue Recognition</i> (ASC 605).&#160; While the standards govern the basis for revenue recognition, significant judgment and the use of estimates are required in connection with the allocation of revenue between product, subscription, services and maintenance revenues, as well as the amount of deferred revenue to be recognized in each accounting period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition Criteria<b>: </b>In general, we recognize revenue when the following criteria have been met:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Persuasive evidence of an arrangement:</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> If we either enter into contracts or receive written purchase orders issued by a customer that legally bind us and the customer, we consider that as persuasive evidence of an arrangement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Delivery</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">: We deem delivery of products to have occurred when the title and risk of ownership have passed to the buyer. Services revenues are considered delivered as they are performed.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Fixed or determinable fee:</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> We consider the fee to be fixed or determinable if the fee is not subject to refund or adjustment and the payment terms are within normal established practices.&#160; If the fee is not fixed or determinable, we recognize revenues as amounts become due and payable with respect to transactions with extended payment terms, or as refund rights lapse with respect to transactions containing such provisions, provided all other revenue recognition criteria have been met.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Collection is deemed probable:</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> We conduct a credit review for all significant transactions at the time of the arrangement to determine the credit-worthiness of the customer.&#160; Collection is deemed probable if we have a reasonable basis to expect that the customer will pay amounts under the arrangement as payments become due.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 48.95pt;text-indent:-24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition for Software Products and Software-Related Services (Software Elements)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Software product revenue</font></i></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">.</font></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; The timing of software product revenue recognition is dependent on the nature of the product sold or the structure of the license.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise Solutions and EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic Solutions: </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue associated with these arrangements, exclusive of amounts allocated to maintenance and other undelivered elements, for which we have vendor-specific objective evidence of fair value (&#147;VSOE&#148;), is recognized upon delivery, provided that all other criteria for revenue recognition have been met.&#160; Revenue associated with term licenses are recognized ratably over the term of the license because we have not established VSOE for post-contract customer support in term license arrangements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Services and maintenance revenues. </font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of our consulting and implementation services are performed under per hour, or fixed fee arrangements.&#160; Revenues from such services are recognized as the services are provided or upon expiration of the contractual service period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Training revenue is either recognized on a per-class basis upon a participant&#146;s attendance or, for those customers who have subscribed to our Annual Training Passport program, revenue is recognized ratably over the annual period.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance revenue includes technical support and software updates on a when-and-if-available basis.&#160; We recognize maintenance revenue ratably over the applicable maintenance period.&#160; We determine the amount of maintenance revenue to be allocated through reference to substantive maintenance renewal provisions contained in multiple element arrangements.&#160; We consider substantive maintenance provisions to be provisions where the cost of the maintenance renewal, stated in the contract with our customer as a percentage of the product fee.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.45pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition for Multiple-Element Arrangements &#151; Software Products and Software-Related Services (Software</font></u><u><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Arrangements)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We often enter into arrangements with customers that purchase both software products and software-related services from us at the same time, or within close proximity of one another (referred to as software-related multiple-element arrangements).&#160; Such software-related multiple-element arrangements may include the sale of our software products, software maintenance services, which include license updates and product support, consulting/implementation services and training whereby the software license delivery is followed by the subsequent delivery of the other elements.&#160; For those software-related multiple-element arrangements, we have applied the residual method to determine the amount of software license revenues to be recognized pursuant to ASC 985-605.&#160; Under the residual method, if VSOE exists for the undelivered elements, this amount is deferred with the remaining, or residual, portion of the arrangement consideration recognized upon delivery of the software license, provided all other revenue recognition criteria are met.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-11<a name="PB_11_125617_2897"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition for Hardware and Subscription Revenues (Nonsoftware Elements)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Hardware product revenue.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> Revenue associated with the sale of forensic hardware is recognized upon shipment to the customers, which include certain resellers, provided that all other criteria for revenue recognition have been met.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Subscription revenue</font></i></b><b><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">.</font></i></b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160; Customers pay subscription fees to access our cloud-based document review and production software; however, they may not take possession of the software at any time during the term of the agreement.&#160; In general, we recognize revenue for subscription fees on a straight-line basis over the contract period commencing on the date the subscription is made available to the customer.&#160; Usage-based fees, which are determined monthly, are recognized when incurred.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition for Multiple-Element Arrangements &#151; Hardware, SaaS and Nonsoftware-Related Services (Nonsoftware Arrangements)</font></u></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We enter into arrangements with customers that purchase both nonsoftware-related SaaS subscription and nonsoftware-related services, such as consulting services, at the same time or within close proximity of one another (referred to as nonsoftware multiple-element arrangements).&#160; Each element within a nonsoftware multiple-element arrangement is accounted for as a separate unit of accounting provided the following criteria are met: the delivered products or services have value to the customer on a standalone basis; and for an arrangement that includes a general right of return relative to the delivered products or services, delivery or performance of the undelivered product or service is considered probable and is substantially controlled by us.&#160; We consider a deliverable to have standalone value if the product or service is sold separately by us or another vendor, or could be resold by the customer.&#160; Further, our revenue arrangements generally do not include a general right of return relative to the delivered products. Where the aforementioned criteria for a separate unit of accounting are not met, the deliverable is combined with the undelivered element and treated as a single unit of accounting for the purposes of allocation of the arrangement consideration and revenue recognition.&#160; For those units of accounting that include more than one deliverable but are treated as a single unit of accounting, we generally recognize revenues ratably over the delivery period.&#160; For the purposes of revenue classification of the elements that are accounted for as a single unit of accounting, we allocate revenue to the respective revenue line items within our consolidated statements of operations based on a rational and consistent methodology utilizing our best estimate of relative selling prices of such elements.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For our nonsoftware multiple-element arrangements, we allocate revenue to each element based on a selling price hierarchy at the arrangement&#146;s inception.&#160; The selling price for each element is based upon the following selling price hierarchy: VSOE, if available; third party evidence (&#147;TPE&#148;) if VSOE is not available; or best estimate of selling price (&#147;BESP&#148;) if neither VSOE nor TPE are available.&#160; A description as to how we determine VSOE, TPE and BESP is provided below:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;"> VSOE</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. VSOE is determined based on its historical pricing and discounting practices for the specific product or service when sold separately.&#160; In determining VSOE, we require that a substantial majority of the selling prices for these services fall within a reasonably narrow pricing range.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;"> TPE</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. When VSOE cannot be established for deliverables in a multiple element arrangement, judgment is applied with respect to whether we can establish a selling price based on TPE.&#160; TPE is determined based on competitor prices for similar deliverables when sold separately.&#160; Generally, our go-to-market strategy differs from that of our peers and our offerings contain a significant level of differentiation such that comparable pricing of services with similar functionality has not been obtained.&#160; Furthermore, we have been unable to reliably determine selling prices of similar competitive services on a stand-alone basis.&#160; As a result, we have not been able to establish selling prices based on TPE.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;"> BESP</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">. When VSOE or TPE cannot be established, we use BESP in our allocation of arrangement consideration. The objective of BESP is to determine the price at which we would transact a sale if the service were sold on a stand-alone basis.&#160; We determine BESP for deliverables by considering multiple factors including but not limited to prices we charge for similar offerings, market conditions, competitive landscape and pricing practices.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-12<a name="PB_12_125650_3020"></a></font></p>
