<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenue Recognition for Multiple-Element Arrangements &#151; Arrangements with Software and Nonsoftware Elements</font></u></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also enter into multiple-element arrangements that may include a combination of our various software-related and nonsoftware-related products and services.&#160; In such arrangements, we first allocate the total arrangement consideration based on the relative selling prices to the software group of elements as a whole and to the nonsoftware group of elements.&#160; We then further allocate consideration allocated to the software group and nonsoftware group to the respective elements within that group following the guidance in ASC 985-605, ASC 605-25, and our policies described above.&#160; After the arrangement consideration has been allocated to the elements, we recognize revenue for each respective element in the arrangement as described above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Deferred Revenue</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Deferred revenue consists primarily of payments received in advance of delivery of products and services associated with the sale of EnCase&#174; product and service offerings including deferral of annual post contract support agreements.&#160; Deferred revenue also includes revenue related to undelivered elements that may or may not have been sold in conjunction with the sale of EnCase&#174; products for which VSOE of the undelivered elements exists.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Research and Development</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We maintain a research and development staff to develop new products and enhance or maintain existing products.&#160; In accordance with <i>Software Industry&#151;Costs of Software to Be Sold, Leased, or Marketed</i> (ASC 985-20) software costs are expensed as incurred until technological feasibility of the software is determined and the recovery of the cost can reasonably be expected, after which any additional costs are capitalized.&#160; To date, we have expensed all software development costs because the establishment of technological feasibility of products and their availability for sale has substantially coincided.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commissions</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although we expense our sales commissions at the time a sale is invoiced to the customer, revenues from certain of our products are recognized over the relevant performance or license period. &nbsp;Accordingly, for those products, we generally experience a delay between when sales commissions are expensed and when we recognize the corresponding revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Leases</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease office facilities under operating leases and certain equipment under capital leases, and account for those leases in accordance with Leases (ASC 840). &#160;For operating leases that contain rent escalation or rent concession provisions, the total rent expense during the lease term is recorded on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease, with the difference between rent payments and the straight-line rent expense recorded as deferred rent in the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Advertising Costs</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Advertising costs are charged to operations as incurred and were $0.6 million as of December 31, 2014, and not significant for other periods presented.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Accounting for Income Taxes</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We account for income taxes in accordance with <i>Income Taxes (ASC 740)</i>.&#160; Deferred income taxes are recorded for the expected tax consequences of temporary differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and amounts recognized for income tax purposes.&#160; We record a valuation allowance to reduce our deferred tax assets to the amount of future tax benefit that is more likely than not to be realized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We account for uncertainty in income taxes in accordance with <i>Income Taxes</i>, which requires companies to determine whether it is more likely than not that a tax position will be sustained upon examination by the appropriate taxing authorities before any part of the benefit can be recorded in the financial statements.&#160; The standard also provides guidance on de-recognition, classification, accounting in interim periods and disclosure requirements for tax contingencies.&#160; In addition, we have applied the standards in determining whether a tax position is effectively settled for the purpose of recognizing previously unrecognized tax benefits.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-13<a name="PB_13_125721_7748"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Foreign Currency Transactions</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies are remeasured at the balance sheet date. Resulting exchange rate gains or losses, which were not material to any years presented, are included as a component of general and administrative expense in current period earnings.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commitments and Contingencies</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We periodically evaluate all pending or threatened litigation and contingencies or commitments, if any, that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on our operations or financial position.&#160; In so doing, we assess the probability of an outcome and determine if it is remote, reasonably possible or probable as defined in accordance with the provisions of <i>Contingency (ASC 450)</i>.&#160; If information available prior to the issuance of our financial statements indicates that it is probable that an asset had been impaired or a liability had been incurred at the date of the financial statements, and the amount of the loss, or the range of probable loss can be reasonably estimated, then such loss is accrued and charged to operations.&#160; If no accrual is made for a loss contingency because one or both of the conditions are not met, but the probability of an outcome is at least reasonably possible, we disclose the nature of the contingency and provide an estimate of the possible loss or range of loss, or state that such an estimate cannot be made.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Testing Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets for Impairment:</font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> In July&nbsp;2012, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) issued Accounting Standards Update No.&nbsp;2012-02,&nbsp;<i>Intangibles&#151;Goodwill and Other (Topic 350)&#151;Testing Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets for Impairment</i>&nbsp;(ASU 2012-02), to allow entities to use a qualitative approach to test indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment. ASU 2012-02 permits an entity to first perform a qualitative assessment to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of an indefinite-lived intangible asset is less than its carrying value.&#160; If it is concluded that this is the case, it is necessary to perform the currently prescribed quantitative impairment test by comparing the fair value of the indefinite-lived intangible asset with its carrying value.&#160; Otherwise, the quantitative impairment test is not required. ASU 2012-02 is effective for us beginning in 2013 and earlier adoption is permitted.&#160; We adopted ASU 2012-02 effective January&nbsp;1, 2013; the adoption of ASU 2012-02 did not have a material impact on our results.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In May&nbsp;2014, the FASB and IASB jointly issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-09, <i>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</i>, which supercedes the revenue recognition requirements in ASC 605 Revenue Recognition.&#160; ASU 2014-09 is a comprehensive new revenue recognition standard that will supercede nearly all existing revenue recognition guidance under US GAAP.&#160; The standard&#146;s core principle is that a company will recognize revenue when it transfers promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the company expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods or services.&#160; In doing so, companies will need to use more judgment and make more estimates than under current authoritative guidance.&#160; These may include identifying performance obligations in the contract, estimating the amount of variable consideration to include in the transaction price and allocating the transaction price to each separate performance obligation.&#160; The standard is effective beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016, and early adoption is not permitted under US GAAP.&#160; We are currently evaluating the financial statement impact of the new revenue recognition standard.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2014, the FASB issued ASU No.&nbsp;2014-15,&nbsp;<i>Presentation of Financial Statements-Going Concern&nbsp;(Subtopic 205-40),&nbsp;Disclosure of Uncertainties about an Entity&#146;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern.</i>&nbsp;This standard sets forth management&#146;s responsibility to evaluate, each reporting period, whether there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern, and if so, to provide related footnote disclosures. The standard is effective for annual and interim reporting periods ending after December&nbsp;15, 2016. &nbsp;We are currently evaluating this new standard and expect it to have no impact on our financial position and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Realignment Expense</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of reducing headcount and consolidating office space during 2014, we have incurred realignment expenses of $3.6 million.&#160; Included in the realignment expense is $3.2 million of severance expense and $0.4 million to accrue for the present value of lease payments for abandoned office space.&#160; The severance costs are included in cost of services and maintenance revenues, selling and marketing, research and development and general and administrative expenses, based on the employees&#146; cost center assignments prior to termination.&#160; Lease abandonment charges are included in general and administrative expenses.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-14<a name="PB_14_125754_141"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note&nbsp;3. Business Combinations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;21, 2012, we acquired CaseCentral Inc., a privately held cloud-based document review and production software-as-a-service provider for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $21.1 million, consisting of $9.6 million in cash (net of $1.4 million in cash acquired), $9.5 million of our common stock, consisting of 849,554 shares valued at the market price of $11.18 per share on the closing date of the transaction, and contingent consideration which had a fair value of approximately $0.6 million as of the closing date of the transaction.&#160; Both the issuance of shares valued at $9.5 million and the contingent consideration of $0.6 million are reflected as noncash activities in the accompanying consolidated statements of cash flows for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with the CaseCentral acquisition, we may be required to pay former CaseCentral shareholders a total of up to $33 million with respect to the three 12-month periods (&#147;earn-out periods&#148;) starting April&nbsp;1, 2012.&#160; The amount of contingent consideration payable with respect to each of the earn-out periods is equal to 35% of certain qualifying CaseCentral SaaS revenues and EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;eDiscovery revenues in excess of $11.1 million during each of the three earn-out periods and is limited to $3.0 million for the first earn-out period, a cumulative total of $13.0 million for the first and second earn-out periods and a cumulative total of $33.0 million for all three earn-out periods.&#160; Any earn-out consideration is payable within 65 days after the end of the applicable earn-out period.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, the fair value of the contingent consideration, which is calculated by summing the present values of various probability-weighted possible outcomes, was estimated to be zero.&#160; We incurred $2.0 million in acquisition-related costs during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 which were expensed as incurred and included in general and administrative expenses.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We acquired CaseCentral to extend our market leadership by delivering a complete and integrated platform solving the e-discovery needs of corporate and government customers. The CaseCentral acquisition closed on February&nbsp;21, 2012 and the results of operations of CaseCentral have been included in the Company&#146;s financial statements subsequent to such date. CaseCentral&#146;s revenues, expenses and net income included in the Consolidated Statements of Operations from the acquisition date through December&nbsp;31, 2012, including amortization of the acquired intangible assets, were as follows (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The assets and liabilities of CaseCentral have been recorded at their estimated fair values at the date of acquisition.&#160; The excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair values of the underlying net tangible and identifiable intangible assets has been recorded as goodwill.&#160; The fair value of net tangible assets other than deferred revenue approximates their carrying values on the date of acquisition.&#160; The fair value assigned to deferred revenue was determined based on estimated costs to fulfill the underlying service obligation.&#160; The fair value assigned to identifiable intangible assets was determined primarily by using a discounted cash flow method.&#160; The acquisition transaction was a stock purchase in which the income tax attributes of CaseCentral carried over to the Company.&#160; The estimated deferred income tax attributes of CaseCentral, after establishment of deferred income tax liabilities associated with the step-up of the fair values of the net assets acquired over their pre-acquisition tax basis, resulted in a net deferred income tax asset.&#160; Given CaseCentral&#146;s history of reporting net losses, our management concluded that realization of the net deferred income tax asset acquired is not likely and therefore a valuation allowance was established to offset the entire net deferred income tax asset.&#160; As a result, deferred income taxes are not reflected in the table below.&#160; The goodwill recognized for CaseCentral is attributable to intangible assets acquired that do not qualify for separate recognition, expected synergies that are projected to increase revenue and profits and an assembled workforce.&#160; The CaseCentral goodwill is not tax deductible.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 4.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net Loss Per Share</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Earnings Per Share </font></i><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(ASC 260) defines unvested share-based payment awards that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends as participating securities that should be included in computing EPS using the two-class method.&#160; The Company&#146;s nonvested restricted stock awards qualify as participating securities.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Basic net loss per common share is calculated by dividing net loss by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the reporting period.&#160; Diluted net loss per share is calculated based on the weighted average number of common shares and dilutive potential common shares outstanding during the period. Dilutive potential common shares consist of the shares issuable upon the exercise of stock options and upon the vesting of restricted stock awards under the treasury stock method.&#160; In net loss periods, basic net loss per share and diluted net loss per share are identical since the effect of potential common shares is anti-dilutive and therefore excluded.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table sets forth the computation of basic and diluted net loss per share (in thousands, except per share data):</font></p>

<td width="21%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border-bottom:double windowtext 2.25pt;border-left:none;border-right:none;border-top:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:21.28%;">
<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14,632</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.88%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We evaluate goodwill for impairment on an annual basis, or more frequently if we believe indicators of impairment exist, by comparing the carrying value of each of our reporting units to their estimated fair value. We have six reporting units: Hardware Products, Software Products, Subscription, Professional Services, Maintenance, and Training.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our goodwill impairment analysis for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 indicated that the estimated fair value of all but one of our reporting units with goodwill was in excess of the carrying value by approximately 140% to over 450%, and are not considered by management to be at risk of failing step one of the impairment test. The estimated fair value of the subscription reporting unit, with $6.9 million of goodwill, exceeded its carrying value by 18%. The significant assumptions that drive the estimated fair value are projected future cash flows, growth rates, and weighted average cost of capital and market multiples. Due to the subjectivity of these assumptions, the subscription reporting unit may be at greater risk for goodwill impairment if actual results differ from our projections or there are significant changes in market and economic factors affecting fair value.&#160; Deterioration in estimated future cash flows in this reporting unit could result in future goodwill impairment. Additionally, one customer represents approximately 47% of our subscription revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; If we were to lose this specific customer, our subscription operations and therefore future cash flows would be adversely affected.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.35pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If a quantitative assessment is necessary a two-step test is performed at the reporting unit level to assess goodwill for impairment. First, the fair value of the reporting unit is compared to its carrying value. If the fair value exceeds the carrying value, the reporting unit is not impaired and no further testing is performed. The second step is performed if the carrying value exceeds the fair value. If the carrying value of the reporting unit exceeds its implied fair value, an impairment loss equal to the difference will be recorded. Indefinite-lived intangible assets are assessed for impairment by comparing the carrying value of the assets with their fair values; however, there were no indefinite-lived intangible assets as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In February&nbsp;2012, the Company acquired CaseCentral resulting in acquired intangible assets. With the exception of customer relationships, which are amortized on a double-declining basis, the acquired intangible assets are being amortized on a straight line basis over their estimated useful lives.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Amortization expense for intangible assets with finite lives was $2.2 million, $2.5 million and $2.4 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&#160; The following table summarizes cumulative amortization expense related to intangible assets subject to amortization as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013 (in thousands):</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table summarizes the estimated remaining amortization expense through the year 2019 and thereafter (in thousands):</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="73%" style="border-collapse:collapse;margin-left:1.0in;width:73.34%;">
<tr>
<td width="78%" valign="bottom" style="border:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:78.88%;">

<p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(320</font></p>    </td>
<td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 2.25pt 0in;width:1.14%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">)</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our foreign income is not a material component of total income (loss) before provision for income taxes.&nbsp; We intend to reinvest the earnings of our non-U.S. subsidiary.&nbsp; Undistributed earnings in our foreign subsidiary are not significant as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our valuation allowance increased by $5.5 million from $35.1 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013 to $40.6 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; Our valuation allowance increased $12.5 million to $35.1 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2013.&#160; We have fully reserved against our deferred tax assets based on our assessment of the future realizability of our deferred tax assets.&#160; In performing these assessments, we consider whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&#160; We consider all available evidence, both positive and negative, including historical levels of income, expectations and risks associated with estimates of future taxable income in assessing the need for a valuation allowance.&#160; A cumulative taxable loss in recent years makes it more difficult for us to realize our deferred tax assets.&#160; We have had three years of cumulative U.S. tax losses and can no longer rely on common tax planning strategies to use U.S. tax losses and we are precluded from relying on projections of future taxable income to support the recognition of deferred tax assets.&#160; As such, the ultimate realization of our deferred tax assets is dependent upon the existence of sufficient taxable income generated in the carryforward periods.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we have federal and state research and development tax credit carryforwards of approximately $4.3 million and $5.2 million, respectively.&#160; The federal tax credits begin to expire in 2026.&#160; The state tax credit carryforward can be carried forward indefinitely.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, our federal and state net operating loss carryforwards for income tax purposes are approximately $72.0 million and $56.0 million, respectively, which expire at various dates through 2034.&nbsp; Our federal and California NOLs have increased significantly as a result of acquired NOL carryforwards through our stock acquisition of CaseCentral Inc. in 2012.&#160; The utilization of NOL carryforwards to reduce taxable income is subject to certain statutory limitations as defined in section 382 of the Internal Revenue Code, as amended.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Included in the NOL deferred tax asset above is approximately $4.0 million of deferred tax asset attributable to excess stock option deductions.&nbsp; Due to a provision within <i>ASC 718, Compensation &#151; Stock Compensation</i>, concerning when tax benefits related to excess stock option deductions can be credited to paid in capital, the related valuation allowance cannot be reversed, even if the facts and circumstances indicate that it is more likely than that the deferred tax asset can be realized.&nbsp; The valuation allowance will only be reversed as the related deferred tax asset is applied to reduce taxes payable.&nbsp; The Company follows <i>Income Taxes (ASC 740)</i> ordering to determine when such NOL has been realized.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We file income tax returns with the Internal Revenue Service, and the taxing authorities of various state and foreign jurisdictions.&#160; We adopted the provisions of accounting for uncertain tax positions in accordance with the <i>Income Taxes (ASC 740) </i>topic on January&nbsp;1, 2007 and, accordingly, performed a comprehensive review of our uncertain tax positions as of that date.&#160; In this regard, an uncertain tax position represents our expected treatment of a tax position taken in a filed tax return, or planned to be taken in a future tax return, that has not been reflected in measuring income tax expense for financial reporting purposes.&#160; A reconciliation of our total unrecognized tax benefits at December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012 follows:</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our unrecognized tax benefit as of December&nbsp;31, 2014 is $1.0 million.&#160; We are subject to routine corporate income tax audits in the United States and foreign jurisdictions.&#160; Due to the net operating loss carryforwards, the Company&#146;s United States federal and state returns are generally open to examination by the Internal Revenue Service and state jurisdictions when such net operating losses are utilized.&#160; Most foreign jurisdictions have statute of limitations that range from three to six years.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since we have fully reserved against our deferred tax assets, the liability for uncertain tax positions is merely a reduction to our deferred tax assets and related valuation allowance which is reflected in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; Any subsequent reduction of the valuation allowance and the recognition of the associated tax benefit would affect our effective tax rate.&#160; Our policy is to recognize interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions, if any, in the income tax provision.&#160; Interest and penalties are computed based upon the difference between our uncertain tax positions under Income Taxes and the amount deducted or expected to be deducted in our tax returns. Due to the overall tax loss position of the Company, we have not accrued or paid for interest and penalties in 2014, 2013 and 2012.&#160; The Company does not expect its uncertain income tax positions to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements within the next twelve months.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 9.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Debt Obligations</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;12, 2012, we entered into a Loan and Security Agreement (as amended or supplemented from time to time, the &#147;Loan Agreement&#148;) with a bank.&nbsp; On October&nbsp;31, 2013, we entered into a modification agreement (&#147;Modification Agreement&#148;) of the Loan Agreement with the bank to modify certain financial covenants pertaining to the Loan Agreement.&nbsp; On September&nbsp;30, 2014, the Loan Agreement expired.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On August&nbsp;29, 2014, we entered into a three year, Senior Secured Revolving Line of Credit (&#147;Revolver&#148;) with another bank.&nbsp; The maximum principal amount that may be outstanding at any given time under the Revolver, which includes up to $3.0 million of standby letters of credit, is $10.0 million.&nbsp; Any borrowings under the Revolver would be collateralized by substantially all of our assets, as well as pledges of capital stock.&nbsp; The Revolver requires that, if we suffer an event of default or have borrowed more than 75% of the maximum principal amount permitted to be outstanding, we maintain an Adjusted Quick Ratio of at least 1.15 to 1.0.&nbsp; If the Adjusted Quick Ratio falls below 1.5 to 1.0, any collections received by the bank on behalf of the Company will be applied to outstanding loan balances before being remitted to the Company&#146;s operating account.&nbsp; The Adjusted Quick Ratio is calculated by dividing Quick Assets (cash less restricted cash plus accounts receivable) by current liabilities (current liabilities plus outstanding standby letter of credit less the current portion of deferred revenue).&nbsp; Borrowings under the Revolver bear interest at a floating rate ranging from 1.25% to 3.25% above the Prime Rate depending on the Company&#146;s Adjusted Quick Ratio.&nbsp; We are obligated to pay a commitment fee of $0.2 million over the three year term of the Revolver. All principal, interest and any other fees will be due and payable in full on or prior to August&nbsp;29, 2017.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we were in compliance with all the covenants of the Revolver.&nbsp; We had letters of credit outstanding against the Revolver in the amount of $1.3 million, resulting in the maximum available borrowing under the Revolver to be $8.5 million.&nbsp; Availability is calculated as 80% of eligible accounts receivable, with a maximum of $10.0 million.&nbsp; To date we have not borrowed under the Revolver.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 10.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Leases</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We lease certain facilities and equipment under non-cancellable operating leases extending through 2024.&#160; The present value of the remaining future minimum lease payments under capital leases is recorded in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; The following is a schedule of future minimum lease payments under capital leases and operating leases (in thousands):</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100.0%;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Rent expense related to operating leases for 2014, 2013 and 2012 was approximately $4.9 million, $6.2 million and $5.2 million, respectively.&#160; During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, we did not have sublease rental income.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 11.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Employee Benefit Plans</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Equity Incentive Plan</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At our 2012 Annual Meeting of Stockholders, our stockholders approved the Second Amendment (the &#147;Second Amendment&#148;) to the Guidance Software,&nbsp;Inc. Second Amended and Restated 2004 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#147;Plan&#148;).&#160; The Second Amendment amended the Plan to: increase the aggregate number of shares of our common stock available for awards under the Plan by an additional 2,500,000 shares, from 9,088,313 shares to a total of 11,588,313 shares; prohibit the re-pricing of stock options and the cancellation of underwater options in exchange for cash payments or other awards, without the approval of our stockholders; provide that shares tendered or withheld to satisfy the grant or exercise price or tax withholding obligation pursuant to any award will count against the limit of shares available for awards under the Plan; and modify the initial and annual equity award grants to our non-employee directors.&#160; The Second Amendment was approved by our Board of Directors in March&nbsp;2012, and approved by our stockholders at our 2012 Annual Meeting of Stockholders on May&nbsp;9, 2012.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2013, approximately 1,535,074 shares were available for grant as options or nonvested restricted stock awards under the Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Stock Options</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The terms of the options granted under the Second Amended and Restated Plan are determined at the time of grant, and generally vest 25% annually over a four-year service period and typically must be exercised within 10 years from the date of grant.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of stock option activity follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We define in-the-money options at December&nbsp;31, 2014 as options that had exercise prices that were lower than the $7.25 fair market value of our common stock at that date.&#160; The aggregate intrinsic value of options outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2014 is calculated as the difference between the exercise price of the underlying options and the fair market value of our common stock for the approximately 3,734,000 options that were in-the-money at that date, of which approximately 584,000 were exercisable.&#160; The total intrinsic value of stock options exercised, determined as of the date of exercise, was $1.1 million, $1.5 million and $3.4 million during the years 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The total grant date fair value of shares vested under such grants during 2014, 2013 and 2012 was $8.3 million, $6.3 million and $4.0 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Share-Based Compensation</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We account for share-based compensation in accordance with Compensation-Stock Compensation (ASC 718).&#160;&#160; Compensation expense for stock options is recognized using the Black-Scholes option pricing model to determine the grant date fair value of share-based payments and recognize that cost, net of an estimated forfeiture rate, as compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the vesting period. Stock awards generally vest 25% annually over a four-year service period.&#160; The determination of the grant date fair value of share-based awards using that model is affected by our stock price as well as assumptions regarding a number of complex and subjective variables. These variables include the estimated number of years that we expect employees to hold their stock options (the option &#147;expected term&#148;) and our expected stock price volatility, risk-free interest rates and dividends to be paid on our stock over that term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">When historical data is available and relevant, the expected term of options granted is determined by calculating the average term from historical stock option exercise experience.&#160; The volatility of our common stock is estimated at the date of grant based on the volatility of our publicly traded common stock over the prior 24 months.&#160; The volatility is calculated based on the adjusted close price each day from a composite index. The risk-free interest rate used in option valuation is based on the implied yield in effect at the time of each option grant, based on US Treasury zero-coupon issues with equivalent</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-23<a name="PB_23_134145_7608"></a></font></p>
<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="left"></div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">expected terms. We use a dividend yield of zero in the Black-Scholes model, as we have no expectation we will pay any cash dividends on our common stock in the foreseeable future. Compensation-Stock Compensation (ASC 718) also requires that we estimate forfeitures at the time of grant and revise those estimates in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. We use historical data to estimate pre-vesting option forfeitures and record share-based compensation expense only for those awards that are expected to vest. Quarterly changes in the estimated forfeiture rate can potentially have a significant effect on reported share-based compensation, as the cumulative effect of adjusting the forfeiture rate for all expense amortization after the grant date is recognized in the period the forfeiture estimate is changed.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, we recorded $0.6 million in additional share-based compensation expense for the accelerated vesting of a certain employee&#146;s restricted stock awards.&#160; The original vesting was to occur during the first quarter of 2015; however, due to the modified terms, the awards vested during the fourth quarter of 2014.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, there was approximately $403,000 of total unrecognized share-based compensation cost related to stock options that is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 4.0 years and approximately $14.5 million of total unrecognized share-based compensation cost related to restricted stock awards that is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.8 years.&#160; We expect to record approximately $6.1 million in share-based compensation in 2015 related to options and restricted stock awards outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Defined Employee Contribution Plans</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a 401(k)&nbsp;plan that allows all full-time eligible employees to contribute up to 75% of their semi-monthly earnings, up to the maximum limit set by the IRS each year.&#160; We match $0.50 on each dollar up to 6% of the employee&#146;s semi-monthly contribution.&#160; Additionally, the Company may make discretionary contributions to the Plan regardless of profitability.&#160; We recorded contribution related expense of approximately $0.9 million, $1.1 million and $1.0 million in the years 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 12.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Stockholders&#146; Equity</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August&nbsp;2008, our Board of Directors authorized a program to repurchase shares of our common stock having an aggregate value of up to $8.0 million.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2014, we had approximately $3.6 million remaining under this authorization.&#160; Acquisitions of shares may be made from time-to-time at management&#146;s discretion, at prevailing prices in the open market, or in privately negotiated transactions, as permitted by securities laws and other legal requirements, and are subject to market conditions and other factors.&#160; For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013, and 2012 we withheld approximately&#160; zero, 284,000, and 207,000 common shares from employees for personal income tax purposes upon the vesting of restricted stock awards. Collectively, these shares are recorded as treasury stock, at cost, in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 13.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fair Value Measurements</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In accordance with <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (ASC 820)</i> for financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis. <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (ASC 820)</i> requires disclosure that establishes a framework for measuring fair value and expands disclosure about fair value measurements. Under this standard, fair value is defined as the price that would be received in exchange for selling an asset or paid to transfer a liability (i.e., the &#147;exit price&#148;) in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. <i>Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures(ASC 820)</i> establishes a hierarchy for inputs used in measuring fair value that minimizes the use of unobservable inputs by requiring the use of observable market data when available. Observable inputs are inputs that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability based on active market data. Unobservable inputs would be inputs that reflect our assumptions about the assumptions market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability based on the best information available in the circumstances. The statement requires fair value measurements be classified and disclosed in one of the following three categories:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="90%" style="border-collapse:collapse;margin-left:24.0pt;width:90.74%;">
<tr>
<td width="9%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:9.78%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level   1:</font></p>    </td>
<td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.74%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>    </td>
<td width="87%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:87.46%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Unadjusted   quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date   for identical, unrestricted assets and liabilities.</font></p>    </td>   </tr>
<tr>
<td width="9%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:9.78%;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Level   2:</font></p>    </td>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Quoted   prices in markets that are not active or financial instruments for which all   significant inputs are observable, either directly or indirectly, and   corroborated by market data.</font></p>    </td>   </tr>
<tr>
<td width="9%" valign="top" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:9.78%;">

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prices   or valuations that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value   measurement and unobservable.</font></p>    </td>   </tr>  </table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Sale of Domain Name</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;1, 2014, we entered into an agreement with one of our vendors, acquiring the rights to distribute certain of their software products, which are to be combined with certain of our own products, in exchange for a domain name owned by the Company.&#160; The term of the agreement extends through December&nbsp;31, 2018, and includes a one-year renewal option for the larger of 1% of the maintenance revenue of certain of the Company&#146;s products, or $450,000.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Market data to determine the fair value of the domain name was not readily available and therefore we used the more clearly evident fair value of the acquired distribution rights to determine the fair value of the agreement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To estimate the fair value of the distribution rights, we developed our own assumptions related to the domain name&#146;s future financial performance and projected maintenance revenue of certain of its products.&#160; We developed various scenarios (base case, downside case, and upside case) and evaluated each case according to the probability of occurrence.&#160; Expected cash flows were determined using the probability weighted average of possible outcomes we expect to occur.&#160; The fair value of the acquired distribution rights was determined to be $0.6 million and was based on the present value of these projected scenarios.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As the domain name had zero book value as of the date of sale, we recorded a gain on the sale of $0.6 million.&#160; The acquired distribution right has been recorded in other assets on the accompanying condensed consolidated balance sheet.&#160; Given the significant unobservable inputs to the calculation, the other asset recognized for the distribution rights falls within Level 3 of the ASC 820 hierarchy, as defined above.&#160; The other asset will be expensed to cost of goods sold ratably over the term of the agreement.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-25<a name="PB_25_140530_7056"></a></font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">CaseCentral Contingent Consideration</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company had obligations, to be paid in cash, to the former shareholders of CaseCentral if certain SaaS revenue thresholds were achieved during the three 12-month periods starting April&nbsp;1, 2012.&#160; The fair value of this contingent consideration was determined using an expected present value technique.&#160; Expected cash flows were determined using the probability - weighted average of possible outcomes that would occur should certain revenue metrics be reached.&#160; There was no market data available to use in valuing the contingent consideration; therefore, the Company developed its own assumptions related to the future financial performance of the businesses to evaluate the fair value of these liabilities.&#160; As such, the contingent consideration was classified within Level 3, as described above.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In connection with estimating the fair value of the contingent consideration, the Company developed various scenarios (base case, downside case, and upside case) and weighted each case according to the probability of occurrence.&#160; The probabilities ranged from 20 percent to 50 percent, with the most significant weighting given to the base case at 50 percent.&#160; These scenarios were developed based on the expected financial performance of CaseCentral, with SaaS revenue growth rates being a primary input in the calculation.&#160; An increase or decrease in the probability of achievement of any of the scenarios could result in a significant increase or decrease to the estimated fair value.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value is reviewed quarterly based on the financial performance of the most recently completed fiscal quarter.&#160; An analysis is performed at the end of each fiscal quarter to compare actual results to forecasted financial performance.&#160; If performance has deviated from projected levels, the valuation is updated for the latest information available.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The significant assumptions that may materially affect fair value are developed in conjunction with the guidance of our senior management to ensure that the most accurate and latest financial projections are used and compared with the most recent financial results in the fair value measurement.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2014 and&#160; December&nbsp;31, 2013, the fair value of the contingent consideration is zero based on forecasted revenues for the remainder of the earn-out period.&#160; As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, the fair value of the contingent consideration current liability is included in the Consolidated Balance Sheets in accrued liabilities and the non-current portion is included in contingent earn-out, net of current portion.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 14.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></b><b><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Contractual Obligations, Commitments and Contingencies</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .65in;text-indent:-.65in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Office Lease</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;26, 2012, we entered into an Office Lease Agreement (the &#147;Lease&#148;) to lease approximately 90,000 rentable square feet of an office building located in Pasadena, California.&#160; The Lease commenced on August&nbsp;1, 2013 and expires May&nbsp;2024.&#160; The Lease allows the Company to consolidate its Pasadena operations into a single location. The total annual rent under the Lease ranges from approximately $2.5 million for the first year to approximately $3.4 million for the final year of the Lease.&#160; The Company has two options to extend the Lease, each for a period of five years.&#160; Leasehold improvements associated with this lease are amortized over the shorter of the expected useful life or lease term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;3, 2014, we entered into an Office Lease Agreement (the &#147;San Francisco Lease&#148;) to lease approximately 6,000 rentable square feet of an office building located in San Francisco, California.&#160; The office building is the new location of our San Francisco office.&#160; The San Francisco Lease commenced on January&nbsp;1, 2015 and expires in January&nbsp;2020.&#160; The total annual rent under the San Francisco Lease ranges from approximately $295,000 for the first year to approximately $332,000 for the final year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Data Center Lease</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective April&nbsp;1, 2014, we entered into a Colocation Lease Agreement (the &#147;Colocation Lease&#148;) to rent space in a building located in Chandler, Arizona.&#160; The Colocation Lease expires on June&nbsp;30, 2018.&#160; The Colocation Lease will serve as our new data center, replacing our former San Francisco location obtained in the Case Central acquisition.&#160; Rent is based on power allocation and ranges from approximately $236,000 for the first year to approximately $265,000 for the final year.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Third-party Software Licenses</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:27.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, the Company entered into a $1.5 million third-party software license agreement that authorizes the Company to integrate database software as a component of its products through November&nbsp;2015.&#160; The agreement also provides for maintenance and support over a two-year period for $0.3 million, which was renewed by the Company after the expiration of the two-year period ending November&nbsp;2014. The $1.8 million was payable in eight quarterly installments of $229,000, with the final installment being paid in January&nbsp;2014.&#160; The license, maintenance and remaining liability have been recorded on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></p>
