<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2014, the Company entered into a $1.5 million third-party software license agreement authorizing the Company to integrate software as a component of its products through March&nbsp;2018.&#160; The agreement also provides for maintenance and support over a three-year period, which may be renewed by the Company at the expiration of the three-year period ending March&nbsp;2018.&#160; The $1.5 million is payable in three annual installments of $492,000, with the final installment being paid in November&nbsp;2016.&#160; The license, maintenance and remaining liability have been recorded on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Legal Matters</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;20, 2011, MyKey Technology Inc. (&#147;MyKey&#148;) filed a complaint against us and certain other parties for patent infringement in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware.&#160; With respect to the Company, the complaint alleged that certain of our data acquisition forensic hardware products that we acquired as a result of our acquisition of certain assets of Tableau, LLC (&#147;Tableau&#148;) infringe three of MyKey&#146;s patents relating to write blocking, duplication and data removal technologies, respectively.&#160; The complaint sought a declaration of infringement, a finding of willful infringement, compensatory damages, treble damages, injunctive relief, interest, expenses, costs and attorneys&#146; fees.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On July&nbsp;22, 2011, MyKey also filed a complaint with the United States International Trade Commission (the &#147;ITC&#148;), alleging infringement by the Company and certain other parties of the three patents discussed in the preceding paragraph and requesting that the ITC commence an investigation pursuant to Section&nbsp;337 of the Tariff Act of 1930.&#160; The complaint sought injunctive relief barring the Company from the importation of products that allegedly infringed the three patents of MyKey.&#160; On August&nbsp;24, 2011, the ITC commenced an investigation of the Company and certain other parties related to the complaint by MyKey.&#160; On August&nbsp;31, 2011 the proceeding in the District Court was stayed pending the resolution of the ITC matter.&#160; On August&nbsp;1, 2012, MyKey amended its ITC complaint to remove allegations that its duplication patent had been infringed by the Company and to reduce the number of claims it alleges the Company has infringed related to MyKey&#146;s data removal patent.&#160; In August&nbsp;2012, the parties completed a trial on the remaining patent claims at issue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;28, 2012, the ITC released a final determination and Order holding that no violation of Section&nbsp;337 of the Tariff Act of 1930 occurred as a result of the Company&#146;s importation into the United States and sale of the products at issue.&#160; This Order effectively ended the ITC proceeding in the Company&#146;s favor.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On February&nbsp;20, 2013, the U.S. District Court of Delaware lifted the stay of the proceedings in the MyKey matter.&#160; Effective April&nbsp;8, 2013, the parties stipulated to a transfer of the matter to the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.&#160; On April&nbsp;16, 2013, the Company filed its Answer and Counterclaim.&#160; MyKey filed a petition to consolidate a number of related cases, including the case against the Company in the Central District of California, into a Multi-District Litigation (&#147;MDL&#148;) proceeding.&#160; On August&nbsp;16, 2013, the MDL panel approved the petition and assigned the MDL consolidated cases to the judge who is also presiding over the individual case against the Company.&#160; The MDL case will dispose of certain issues common to the consolidated cases, such as the validity of patents being asserted against the joint defendants.&#160; On May&nbsp;23, 2014, the parties completed a Markman hearing related to claim construction of the patents at issue.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On March&nbsp;26, 2014, MyKey also filed a complaint against the United States of America alleging that the United States has infringed U.S. Patents No.&nbsp;6,813,682, 7,159,086 and 7,228,379 by or through its acceptance, receipt and/or use of write blocker products, data duplication products and data removal products.&#160; The complaint alleges that such products were supplied to the government by the Company and certain of its co-defendants in the MDL proceeding.&#160; No damages amount is stated in the complaint.&#160; The government could assert a claim for indemnification against the Company but has not done so yet.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;16, 2014, MyKey filed a Notice of Status on Claim Construction Issues in which it acknowledged that MyKey will not be able to prove that the Company&#146;s data duplication products infringed U.S. Patent 7,159,086.&#160; In the same filing, MyKey acknowledged that certain claims of United States Patent 6,813,682 are invalid and therefore cannot be infringed by any product.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-27<a name="PB_27_140708_5796"></a></font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We intend to defend the remaining MyKey matters vigorously and, at this time, are unable to estimate what, if any, liability we may have in connection with these matters.&#160; Although a financial loss is reasonably possible from currently pending MyKey cases, the Company is unable to estimate a range of reasonably possible financial losses due to various reasons, including, among others, that (1)&nbsp;certain of the proceedings are still at an early stage, (2)&nbsp;there is uncertainty as to the outcome of pending appeals, motions, or settlements, (3)&nbsp;there are significant factual issues to be resolved, (4)&nbsp;there are unresolved negotiations with certain indemnitors or indemnitees of the Company, related to the actions, and (5)&nbsp;we have meritorious defenses that we intend to assert.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, we may become involved in various other lawsuits and legal proceedings that arise in the ordinary course of business.&#160; Litigation is subject to inherent uncertainties, and an adverse result in these or other matters may arise from time to time that may harm our business.&#160; We are not currently aware of any such other legal proceedings or claims that are likely to have a material impact on our business.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Indemnifications</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have agreed to indemnify our directors and executive officers for costs associated with any fees, expenses, judgments, fines and settlement amounts incurred by them in any action or proceeding to which any of them is, or is threatened to be, made a party by reason of his or her services in their role as a director or officer.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Sales Tax Liabilities</font></i></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s sales and use tax filings are subject to customary audits by authorities in the jurisdictions where it conducts business in the United States, which may result in assessments of additional taxes.&#160; In March&nbsp;2011, we determined that additional sales taxes were probable of being assessed by a certain state as a result of the preliminary findings specific to a sales and use tax audit.&#160; The balance for the years in which the statute of limitation has not expired is approximately $1.2 million, including interest of approximately $0.4 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2014.&#160; The estimated incremental sales and use tax liability was based on a similar model that was being used by the state conducting the sales and use tax audit.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Should other states where we have not imposed sales and use taxes determine that the sale of our products or services are subject to sales and use taxes, we could incur future assessments, which would require charges to operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Note 15.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Segment Information</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We apply the guidance in Segment Reporting (ASC 280) based on our internal organization and reporting of revenue and other performance measures.&#160; Our segments are designed to allocate resources internally and provide a framework to determine management responsibility.&#160; Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise about which discrete financial information is available that is evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision maker, or decision making group, in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance.&#160; Our chief operating decision maker is our Chief Executive Officer.&#160; We have five operating segments, as summarized below:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Products segment&#151; Includes EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Enterprise, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Cybersecurity, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;&#160; </font>Analytics, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;eDiscovery, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Forensic, EnCase<font style="position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>&#160;Portable, Premium License Support Program and hardware sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Subscription segment&#151; Includes subscription services for cloud-based document review and production software.&#160; The subscription segment was new as of February&nbsp;2012 due to our acquisition of CaseCentral.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Professional services segment&#151; Performs consulting services and implementations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Training segment&#151; Provides training classes by which we train our customers to effectively and efficiently use our software products.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Maintenance segment&#151; Provides software updates, telephone and email support.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 42.5pt;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:25.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Currently, we do not separately allocate operating expenses to these segments, nor do we allocate specific assets, with the exception of goodwill, to segments.&#160; Therefore, the segment information reported includes only revenues, cost of revenues and segment profit.&#160; The following tables present the results of operations for each operating segment (in thousands):</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, long-lived assets located in the United States, net of accumulated depreciation and amortization was approximately $14.4 million and $18.2 million, respectively.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2014, 2013 and 2012, long-lived assets located in foreign countries, net of accumulated depreciation and amortization was approximately $0.2 million, $0.2 million, and $0.3 million, respectively.&#160; No individual country outside of the United States accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated long-lived assets.&#160; Long-lived assets exclude goodwill and intangibles assets, which are not allocated to specific geographies as it is impracticable to do so.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:24.5pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues from transactions with the U.S. Government were generated across all reporting segments and were greater than 10% of total revenues.&#160; U.S. Government revenues were $19.8 million and $14.7 million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2014 and 2013, respectively.</font></p>
